methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Navier is a seed-stage transportation company founded by Sampriti Bhattacharyya that has raised $7.2M to date. The broader transportation sector comp universe includes six private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, EarthGrid, Olympian Motors) and no public comparables, though peer-level valuation triangulation proved constrained by stage and tier dispersion within the Transportation sector.

Stage-progression methodology was the primary applicable valuation approach, applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $7.2M raised as a proxy baseline, yielding $18M. Peer-median comparison was not feasible: while three transportation peers exist in the wider dataset, none qualified as same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier matches after filtering, falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold needed for reliable cohort analysis. Reliance on all-sector median would risk material distortion given stage and business model heterogeneity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $21M (median $18M), with the narrowness of this range reflecting dependence on a single method rather than robust triangulation. Primary valuation uncertainty stems from the absence of tight peer comparables at seed stage in transportation and the significant variance in exit multiples and growth profiles across the wider comp set. Additional clarity on capital deployment efficiency, market traction metrics, and competitive positioning within the transportation subsector would sharpen subsequent rounds of analysis.
